title: Chicago, summer 1835

lighting.note: Early afternoon, 1 July 1835. Sun azimuth and elevation are computed from this time and the datum lat/lon and drive both sky and the single directional light. Chosen so the south elevation is genuinely lit — at this latitude in July the sun is high, so vertical surfaces take light at a grazing angle and a mid-morning sun leaves a south wall too dark to read its documented white paint.

anchors.note: T-0224. The public square is the one platted block the town held in common (blk_randolph_lasalle, data/reconstruction/1835_reserved_ground.json) and it carries the county's only three public buildings, and until this anchor a visitor was offered no way to stand on it. NOT ONE NUMBER HERE IS AUTHORED. The block's inside corners are the ones data/structures/log_jail.json derives and quotes (UTM 447538.25/4637130.78 NW through 447639.80/4637018.05 SE); through data/datum.json those are local (465.55, -265.02) NW and (567.10, -377.75) SE, and the stand is 6 m inside the Clark-and-Washington corner. Ground 0.875 m on the committed heightfield, which is flat to 0.04 m across the whole block. The bearing is the BISECTOR of the two buildings the stand is there to carry: the estray pen at the south-west corner bears 266.6 deg and the log jail at the north-west corner 316.9 deg, so each sits 25.2 deg off centre, inside the 28.2 deg half-frame a 390x780 phone actually draws. THE 1835 COURT-HOUSE IS NOT IN THIS FRAME and no stand on this block can hold all three - they sit on three different corners of a 101 x 112 m block, so their angular spread from anywhere on it is over 90 deg against a 56 deg mobile frame, and standing back far enough to gather them would put every one past 200 m. What the frame is FOR is the ground: T-0027 replanted this block as sedge meadow and nothing in this project could show that in a picture.

note: The first scene. Population roughly 3,265 in the late-1835 count; the town is twenty months old and has grown roughly tenfold in two years. Wabansia and Kinzie's Addition are platted (the Wooley correction was approved 17 June 1835, two weeks before this date) but almost entirely unbuilt. Anchor coordinates are provisional until the datum is verified — they are placeholders in the same local frame, not survey positions. Spawn and the near anchors are now derived from the Sauganash's real placement at Lake and Market — about 100 m east and 130 m south of the forks confluence — rather than from the datum origin, which is in the middle of the river. Both anchors that once pointed at a surveyed corner because their records had not landed have now resolved onto it: Green Tree stands at Lake and Canal looking east at the tavern, and South Water stands in the street at Wells. The South Water anchor was moved there on 2026-08-15 from (260, -95), which was 101 m south of the centreline of the street it is named for and framed a field. Its easting is the Wells corner the South Water records are themselves offset from (OpenStreetMap E 447402.5, N 4637411.6, the West Upper Wacker Drive / North Wells junction, quoted in those records' position notes); its northing is the committed South Water centreline at that easting (data/streets/1835.json), which sits about 9 m south of the modern junction centre because the 1835 line is shifted into the dry half of the platted riverfront corridor. A camera is not a placement, and this one claims nothing about a building. The forks anchor moved from (-20, -30) to (-100, -28) once the river channel was traced: the placeholder stood in the middle of the South Branch. It is now on the west bank at Wolf Point, which is what the name meant, looking east across the confluence and down the main stem. The wharf anchor (2026-08-18, T-0041) stands on the bank 3.6 m out of Newberry & Dole's river wall, looking down the waterward normal of the dock the wharf layer draws there — the ground at that point is 0.38 m above the water plane, so it is a stand on the bank and not on the deck, which is not a walk surface.
